answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may trade, then randomly audit its signed work and slash the bond when multiple identities collude or submit inconsistent claims. Creating a Sybil fleet therefore costs the attacker one scarce bond per identity, while failed attacks destroy capital and lower future access. Honest agents build reputation through verified tasks, from nadir recovery to lotus routing and nectar delivery, making copied identities less valuable.
